chapter.heading: Living in Desert Hideouts
chapter.v:
One day
David heard the news, “The Philistines are attacking Keilah and stealing the grain from the threshing floors.”

So he
asked advice from the Lord, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?”The Lord told David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”

But David's
men told him, “Even here in Judah we feel afraid. If we went to Keilah to fight the Philistine armies we'd be absolutely terrified!”

So David
asked advice from the Lord again, and the Lord told him, “Go immediately to Keilah, for I will give you victory over the Philistines.”

Then David
and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. They slaughtered them and drove off their livestock. By doing this David saved the people of Keilah.

(When Abiathar,
son of Ahimelech, ran away to David at Keilah he brought the ephod with him.)

When Saul
found out that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has handed him over to me, because he has locked himself inside a town with gates that can be barred shut.”

So Saul
called up his whole army to go and attack Keilah and to besiege David and his men.

When David
learned that Saul was plotting to attack him, he asked Abiathar the priest, “Please bring the ephod.”

David prayed,
“Lord, God of Israel, I your servant have been clearly told that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.

Are the
town leaders of Keilah going to hand me over to him? Is Saul going to come, as I have heard? Lord, God of Israel, please tell me.”“Yes, he'll come,” the Lord replied.

“And will
the town leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?” David asked.“Yes, they will,” the Lord replied.

So David
and his men, who numbered around six hundred, left Keilah and moved around from place to place. When Saul discovered that David had escaped from Keilah, he didn't bother going there.

David set
up camp in the wilderness strongholds, staying in the mountains of the Desert of Ziph. Saul searched for him continually, but God did not let David be captured.

While David
was staying at Horesh in the Desert of Ziph, he found out that Saul was on his way to murder him.

Saul's son
Jonathan went to see David in Horesh and encouraged him to go on trusting in God, telling him,

“Don't worry,
because my father Saul is never going to find you. You're going to be king of Israel, and I'll be your deputy. Even my father Saul knows this.”

The two
of them made an agreement before the Lord. David stayed in Horesh and Jonathan went home.

Then the
people of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and told him, “David is hiding in our area, in the strongholds in Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, in the southern wastelands.

So, Your
Majesty, please come whenever you want, and we'll make sure to hand him over to you.”

“The Lord
bless you for thinking about me,” Saul replied.

“Please go
and make absolutely sure you know exactly where he is—where he stays and who has seen him there—because people tell me that he's very devious.

Look for
and mark down all his hiding places. Then come back to me when you're sure, and I'll go back with you. If he's here in the country, I will hunt him down among all the people of Judah.”

So the
people of Ziph set off, returning to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the Desert of Maon in the Arabah Valley in the southern wastelands.

Saul and
his men started hunting for him. When David found out, he went down to the rock, and stayed in the Desert of Maon. When Saul heard this, he chased after David in the Desert of Maon.

Saul was
traveling along one side of the mountain, while David and his men were on the other side, rushing to get away. But just as Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men, about to capture them,

a messenger
arrived to tell Saul, “Come at once! The Philistines have invaded the country!”

So Saul
had to stop chasing David and went to confront the Philistines. That's why the place is called the “Rock of Escape.”

Then David
left and went to live in the strongholds of En-gedi.
